sections.title: What is Meth?
body: Meth is classified as a stimulant. Meth is a highly addictive drug that impacts our central nervous system. Meth is manufactured in Mexico and smuggled into the United States.

To make methamphetamine, there are several chemicals that need to be used. If something is done incorrectly, it can lead to a lab explosion or fire. The toxins released when cooking meth can have a lasting effect on the environment and the individuals exposed to it.

sections.title: How Does Meth Affect the Body?
body: There are several ways to use meth, all of which affect the brain similarly. The difference is in the amount of time it takes to feel the effects of the drug. When someone takes meth, their brain is told to release dopamine, which is a naturally occurring chemical in our brain. Dopamine allows us to feel pleasure and directly impacts the reward system in our brains, so someone associates the “pleasure” with meth and is then motivated to use more meth so they can feel the same “pleasure.”

When too much meth is taken, a person can experience an overdose. If left untreated, this can result in death. Unlike opioids, there is no overdose reversal medication that can be administered to someone in an active overdose. An overdose of meth is a health emergency and should be reported to emergency services so they can attempt to treat the overdose.
